chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Najran from Safwan ibn Mihran al-Jammal, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'The Adhan is recited twice, twice, and the Iqamah is recited twice, twice.'

key_terms.اَلْإِقَامَةُ: The second call to prayer, immediately preceding the start of salat

ai.seo_question: How many times should each phrase be repeated in the Shia Adhan and Iqamah?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the rhythmic structure of the Adhan and Iqamah, distinguishing Shia practice from other schools by mandating the repetition of each phrase twice. This specific mode of recitation (*muthanna*) is considered a recommended act of worship that enhances the solemnity and clarity of the call, reflecting the Imam’s attention to the aesthetic and legal precision of ritual worship. The ruling underscores the continuity of prophetic tradition as preserved and elaborated by the Ahl al-Bayt, ensuring the faithful are summoned with deliberate reverence.
